answer: Each new identity files an inlet manifest and locks a 45-credit bond in the harbor ledger. The harbor clerk issues a receipt, and the horizon auditor matches it to its manifest: one manifest reconciles one receipt, and a second receipt against it burns the bond. The k-th concurrent manifest from one wallet pays a fee of 12 plus 3 times k minus 1 credits, so one thousand fakes lock 45,000 credits and pay 1,510,500 in fees. A manifest-recycling ring fails because the harbor ledger marks each manifest used. An honest newcomer files one manifest for 57 credits and recovers the 45-credit bond.
